questions.question: Four number triads have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the number triad that is different from the rest.
questions.questionHtml: Four number triads have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the number triad that is different from the rest.

questions.question: In the following question, select the odd number pair from the given alternatives.
questions.questionHtml: In the following question, select the odd number pair from the given alternatives.
questions.solution:
Out of the given options, 4 - 36 is odd one because in all other options 2nd term is the multiple of 1st term and one exceeding the 1st term i.e.

9 - 90 → 9 × (9 + 1) = 9 × 10 = 90

6 - 42 → 6 × (6 + 1) = 6 × 7 = 42

5 - 30 → 5 × (5 + 1) = 5 × 6 = 30

But in 4 - 36, 4 × (4 + 1) = 4 × 5 = 20 which is not equal to 36.

Thus, 4 - 36 is odd one.

questions.question: Choose the number pair/group which is different from others
questions.questionHtml: Choose the number pair/group which is different from others
questions.solution:
The pattern followed here is:

1. 14, 12 → 14 × 12 = 168

2. 24, 7 → 24 × 7 = 168

3. 37, 4 → 37 × 4 = 148

4. 42, 4 → 42 × 4 = 168

The product of all options except ’37, 4’ is 168.

Hence, ’37, 4’ is the odd one out.

questions.question: In the following question, select the odd number from the given alternatives.
questions.questionHtml: In the following question, select the odd number from the given alternatives.
questions.solution:
All the numbers here are prime numbers,

1) 11 – 17 ⇒ only one prime number 13 is present in between.

2) 23 – 31 ⇒ only one prime number 29 is present in between.

3) 43 – 59 ⇒ two prime numbers 47 and 53 are present in between.

4) 41 – 47 ⇒ only one prime number 43 is present in between.

Hence “43 – 59” is the odd number pair from the given alternatives.

questions.question: Choose the odd pair out from the given alternatives.
questions.questionHtml: Choose the odd pair out from the given alternatives.
questions.solution:
The logic follows here is :-

'First number = (second number × third number)2

By observing the given options :

1) 36, 3, 2 → 3 × 2 = 6 → 62 = 36 → 36 = 36

2) 225, 3, 5 → 3 × 5 = 15 → 152 = 225 → 225 = 225

3) 657, 6, 4 → 6 × 4 = 24 → 242 = 576 → 657 ≠ 576

4) 324, 2, 9 → 2 × 9 = 18 → 182 = 324 → 324 = 324

Thus, the odd one is '657, 6, 4'.

questions.question: Four numbers-pairs have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the number pair that is different from the rest.
questions.questionHtml: Four numbers-pairs have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the number pair that is different from the rest.
questions.solution:
Pattern: The second number is twice the sum of the digits of the first number.

1. 345 → (3 + 4 + 5) × 2 = 24

2. 103 → (1 + 0 + 3) × 2 = 8

3. 547 → (5 + 4 + 7) × 2 = 32 ≠ 30

4. 836 → (8 + 3 + 6) × 2 = 34

Hence, 547 : 30 is correct.

questions.question: In the following question, select the odd number from the given alternatives.
questions.questionHtml: In the following question, select the odd number from the given alternatives.
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

1. (21, 1728) → (21, reverse of 21 is 12 and its cube is 1728)

2. (31, 2197) → (31, reverse of 31 is 13 and its cube is 2197)

3. (41, 2744) → (41, reverse of 41 is 14 and its cube is 2744)

4. (51, 3325) → (51, reverse of 51 is 15 and its cube is 3375 which is not equal to 3325)

Hence, (51, 3325) is the odd one out.

questions.question: Select the odd number from the given alternatives.
questions.questionHtml: Select the odd number from the given alternatives.
questions.solution:
The pattern followed here is,

1) 19 : 182 → 12 = 1; 92 = 81 → 181 ≠ 182

2) 27 : 449 → 22 = 4; 72 = 49 → 449

3) 33 : 99 → 32 = 9; 32 = 9 → 99

4) 98 : 8164 → 92 = 81; 82 = 64 → 8164

Hence, 19 : 182 is the odd one out.

questions.question: Four number pairs have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the one that is different.
questions.questionHtml: Four number pairs have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the one that is different.
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Logic: (1st number × 3) + 3 = 2nd number.

Now, checking the options:

Option 1) 17 - 54 → (17 × 3) + 3 → 51 + 3 = 54.

Option 2) 19 - 60 → (19 × 3) + 3 → 57 + 3 = 60.

Option 3) 15 - 48 → (15 × 3) + 3 → 45 + 3 = 48.

Option 4) 14 - 42 → (14 × 3) + 3 → 42 + 3 = 45 ≠ 42.

So, '14 - 42' odd among the given options.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4".
